item.title: Dynamic Table of Contents
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
About this page

This page is long on purpose. The table of contents in the left column lists the headings on the page and highlights the section you are reading as you scroll. Select an entry to jump to its section.

The table stays in view while you read because the block uses sticky positioning, and the column it sits in is as tall as the article.

How the list is built

The block renders an empty list on the server. When the page loads, its script collects the headings inside the post content and adds a link to each one, in the order they appear.

Because the list is built from the page itself, there is nothing to update by hand when you add, remove or rename a heading.

Heading anchors

Each link points at an id on its heading. The plugin adds one to every Heading block that has no HTML anchor, made from the heading text, so you never have to set anchors by hand.

A heading that already has an anchor keeps it, so existing links to that section keep working.

Heading levels

The block's Include H1 headings to Include H6 headings settings choose which levels are listed. This one lists H2 and H3 headings only, so the level-four heading below this section is left out.

The list is flat: every entry has the same indent, whatever the level of its heading.

A level-four heading

Switch on Include H4 headings in the block's settings and this heading joins the list, in document order with the rest.

Use them for small subsections, such as the steps of a longer section.

Highlighting the current section

As you scroll, the entry for the heading in the top quarter of the window is shown in bold, so you can see where you are on the page.

Scroll back up and the highlight moves back to the earlier entries.

Sticky placement

Sticky positioning is one of the block's settings. It keeps the table in view while the rest of its column scrolls past.

The column has to be taller than the table for this to work. Here, the article in the right-hand column sets the height of both columns.

Styling

The block supports text and background colors, padding, margin, block spacing and borders. This one has a background color and padding.

Its title, On this page, is edited in place like any other text. Clear it and the block shows no title.

A heading left out of the list

The heading above has Hide from table of contents switched on in its settings, so it is not listed. The toggle adds the hide-from-toc class; give that class to a Group or Column and every heading inside it is left out.

Use it for headings that label a part of the page but are not a section of their own, such as a heading inside a call-to-action box.

Headings inside other blocks

Some blocks, such as the Accordion below, render their own headings. The block's Include headings nested in other blocks setting is on, so these headings are listed too.

Yes. The list is built from the page each time it loads, so it always matches the published content.

Yes. Switch on the levels you want in the block's settings, such as Include H2 headings. This page lists H2 and H3. In code, the a8csp_dynamic_table_of_contents_heading_selectors filter can change which headings are collected.

Wrapping up

That is the end of the page. Scroll back up and watch the highlight in the table of contents follow you.

To try it yourself, open this page in the editor, add a heading anywhere in the article, and view the page again: the new heading is in the list.

You can also change the title of the table, or turn off Include headings nested in other blocks to see the Accordion headings drop out of the list.
